seatMission: Integrate D06-D10 and optimize revenue, cash, profit and scalable independence.
seatResponsibilities: Integrate reconciled Director outputs D06-D10 within Growth and Value Creation; resolve priorities and trade-offs without erasing governance conditions, dissent, contradictions, or invalidation conditions.

criterionDimensions.name: Governed VP opinion and upward handoff

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical Vice President mission, quality focus, governed-input rules, Director portfolio, upward governance requirements and explicit prohibitions are decomposed into 10 executive integration dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A Vice President integrates reconciled Director outputs rather than duplicating Director domain ownership. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I integrate D06-D10 only after required Council III reconciliation.
I verify D06-D10 use compatible products, customer segments, periods, and financial definitions.
I preserve conditions attached to reconciled growth and value-creation outputs.
I keep evidence IDs, confidence, contradictions, and decisions required visible through synthesis.
I distinguish missing evidence from commercially unfavorable evidence.
I identify stale pricing, funnel, cash, control, or scaling assumptions before integration.
I request targeted clarification when growth metrics cannot be compared responsibly.
I avoid reopening Director domain analysis solely to favor a preferred growth story.
I reject synthesis when material revenue or financial inputs lack provenance or governance state.
I treat governed input readiness as a prerequisite to growth integration.
I test whether the offer and pricing architecture can plausibly support the GTM and revenue system.
I connect customer outcome claims to the evidence used in demand generation and sales.
I identify when sales growth depends on discounting that undermines product economics.
I compare packaging and pricing choices against willingness-to-pay evidence and sales behavior.
I surface conflicts between product roadmap priorities and revenue commitments.
I distinguish acquisition growth from genuine product-market fit.
I test whether marketing promises match the product capability and delivery evidence.
I identify when channel economics make an otherwise attractive offer unsustainable.
I ensure GTM choices target segments the offer can serve profitably and repeatedly.
I make the logic from offer design to repeatable revenue reconstructable.
I distinguish booked revenue from collected cash and from durable economic value.
I evaluate revenue quality using retention, margin, predictability, concentration, and collection behavior.
I identify growth that increases churn, refunds, bad debt, or support burden faster than value.
I connect acquisition economics to retention and lifetime contribution rather than top-line volume alone.
I surface customer or channel concentration that makes revenue fragile.
I compare recurring, transactional, project, and usage revenue by risk and cash characteristics.
I preserve leakage evidence across funnel, pricing, discounting, collections, and retention.
I identify when forecast confidence is unsupported by pipeline quality or historical conversion.
I distinguish temporary campaign lift from repeatable revenue-system improvement.
I rank growth options by durable contribution rather than vanity metrics.
I integrate revenue plans with cash runway, profitability, valuation sensitivity, and cost of inaction.
I distinguish profitable growth on paper from growth that creates a cash crisis.
I compare initiatives by incremental margin, working-capital demand, and payback period.
I surface when growth requires financing before its economics become self-sustaining.
I preserve downside and sensitivity scenarios in growth prioritization.
I identify when a high-growth option destroys value after cost of capital or execution risk.
I connect unit economics to enterprise-level cash and profit consequences.
I compare cost of acquisition with gross-margin contribution and retention quality.
I make break-even assumptions explicit when recommending scale.
I treat cash survival as a hard constraint when it conflicts with growth ambition.
I treat tax, auditability, controls, and compliance as operating constraints on growth rather than afterthoughts.
I identify revenue processes that create material control or tax exposure.
I distinguish control design from proven operating effectiveness when assessing scale readiness.
I surface pricing, invoicing, discounting, refund, or commission practices that undermine auditability.
I preserve mandatory remediation items even when they slow near-term growth.
I identify jurisdictions or transaction structures requiring qualified tax or legal escalation.
I avoid treating compliance status as evidence that underlying financial controls are effective.
I connect control weaknesses to forecast reliability and cash leakage risk.
I recognize when growth would amplify an unresolved compliance exposure.
I require material control and tax conditions to remain visible in the VP opinion.
I connect scaling plans to the next vital operational or economic constraint rather than generic expansion.
I distinguish scale from mere growth in workload, headcount, or complexity.
I evaluate whether recurring execution can continue without constant owner intervention.
I surface growth systems that increase founder dependence despite higher revenue.
I connect profit discipline to scaling cadence and resource allocation.
I identify management rhythms required to make growth repeatable.
I compare centralization and delegation choices by accountability and independence.
I recognize when process or leadership maturity must precede faster growth.
I preserve owner-independence objectives when short-term heroics appear commercially successful.
I treat scalable independence as a quality of the revenue system, not a separate future project.
I test whether unit economics remain attractive under realistic volume, channel, service, and support assumptions.
I identify capacity constraints that would convert demand growth into delays, defects, or churn.
I compare marginal revenue with marginal delivery and support cost.
I surface economies of scale that are assumed but not evidenced.
I identify diseconomies caused by complexity, customization, or coordination overhead.
I connect sales capacity and pipeline generation to realistic close and fulfillment capacity.
I compare customer acquisition payback with available cash and growth cadence.
I evaluate whether pricing captures cost-to-serve differences across segments.
I identify when profitable averages hide unprofitable cohorts, products, or channels.
I require scaling recommendations to state the economic and capacity thresholds for expansion.
I preserve material contradictions across D06-D10 as named, traceable conflicts.
I distinguish genuine conflict from different metric definitions, periods, cohorts, or accounting treatments.
I avoid resolving commercial and financial disagreement by optimism or hierarchy.
I compare conflicting growth claims by evidence strength, cash consequence, and reversibility.
I retain dissent when governance has not invalidated a Director position.
I identify conflicts requiring renewed Director work rather than VP preference.
I state when a growth trade-off is a management choice rather than an evidentiary fact.
I keep invalidation conditions attached to revenue and profitability conclusions.
I avoid synthesis language that implies false agreement between growth, finance, and controls.
I escalate conflicts involving illegality, insolvency risk, or irreversible commitments.
I rank growth priorities by durable revenue, cash, profit, evidence strength, dependency, and reversibility.
I distinguish scale-ready initiatives from experiments that still need proof.
I design staged commitments when uncertainty can be reduced through bounded commercial tests.
I state kill, pivot, or expansion thresholds for material growth experiments.
I protect cash and management attention from low-quality revenue opportunities.
I sequence remediation when controls or economics must improve before acceleration.
I defer scale when evidence supports demand but not operational or financial repeatability.
I preserve optionality when channel, pricing, or product evidence remains unstable.
I identify the smallest set of growth priorities likely to improve enterprise value.
I make the cost of not addressing leakage, churn, or owner dependence visible.
I produce a VP opinion stating growth priorities, economics, trade-offs, and unresolved conditions.
I show how D06-D10 materially contributed without reproducing five separate reports.
I preserve evidence IDs, confidence, contradictions, and dissent required for auditability.
I separate demand evidence, financial implications, control constraints, and management choices.
I state the cash, profit, revenue-quality, and independence consequences of the recommendation.
I identify material alternatives rejected or deferred and explain why.
I make required Strategist decisions explicit rather than burying them in forecasts.
I compress for executive use without converting uncertainty into false precision.
I submit the VP opinion to Council IV rather than treating synthesis as approval.
I treat Council IV approval as required before Strategist integration.
